newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas up sharply in volatile market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas up sharply in volatile market.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices continued to climb Tuesday, as cold weather blanketed most of the Midwest and southern U.S. Plains, sources said.
Gulf prices, which for the most part following the lead of NYMEX, rose an average of 40 cents to the low-$4.40s, with deals reported done from the $4.30s to the $4.50s.
Temperatures in the producing region, including southern Texas, were about 20 to 30 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal, causing buyers to scramble for swing gas.
In south Texas, the market ranged from the $4.20s to about $5, with the bulk of the business done in the low-$4.40s.
Although temperatures in the producing region are expected to moderate as the week progresses, they are expected to remain well below-normal through the early part of next week.

In the market areas, New York city-gate prices jumped into the $4.70-4.80 range early following Monday's NYMEX rally but then eased to about $4.60 as futures fell, which is mostly unchanged from Monday.
The New York Power Authority's 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear power unit, shut this weekend for repairs, will likely restart later this week.
Appalachian prices ranged anywhere from the mid-$4.30s to the $4.80s, depending on the time of the deal. Sources said most gas was traded in the $4.45-4.50 range, up about 20 cents from Monday.

Arctic weather swept through the Midcontinent, pushing prices up as much as $1.00. Amid volatile swings in the market, traders said most trades were in the $4.60-4.65 range, up about 60 cents from Monday.
Temperatures in the region are expected to remain at least 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal through the weekend, with the coldest temperatures forecast for the northern plains.
In west Texas, where consumers are coping with temperatures about 10-20 degrees below-normal, Permian gas prices continued their climb to surpass the $5 mark early today.
Most Permian deals were confirmed done in the low-$4.80s, traders said.
The thermometer is expected to drop to as much as 30 degrees below-normal by Wednesday in Texas, dragging temperatures below freezing.
At the southern California border, the market ranged anywhere from the $4.50s to the $4.70s, with most quotes in the high-$4.60s.
Temperatures in the Southwest for the remainder of the week are forecast to remain four to eight degrees below-normal in the western half and as much as 15 degrees below-normal in the east.
